comment: What the real hardware does, measured rather than assumed.
The simulated glasses are built from these numbers, so a test that passes
against the simulation is a test against something the device was actually
seen doing. Where a value here is wrong, the simulation is wrong in the
same direction, which is the point: it fails honestly rather than passing
against an invention.
Every measurement carries the power state it was taken in, because on this
hardware that changes the answer. The phone was on its own battery, low,
with the battery saver on — the worst case, and the one worth pinning.
Re-measure on a charger and the timings should improve; the shapes should
not.
Re-taking these: tools/measure_device.sh, with the glasses attached.
Read every other number in this file against this one. The battery saver
turns itself on at the level the owner chose — 40% here — and its policy
includes quick doze and disabling optional sensors.
The glasses draw their power from the phone over the same cable that
carries the video, so a session on battery is a session on a battery that
is being drained twice.
Eight cores in three tiers, which is why splitting work evenly across
them is the wrong shape: an even split finishes when the slowest core
finishes its eighth. The maximum frequencies were not capped by the
battery saver in this reading — the low current frequencies are idle,
not a throttle — but scheduling and thermal headroom still differ, so
the split is re-measured when the power state changes rather than
decided once.
The USB identity the driver opens, and the pose stream it gets back.
The pose rate is counted rather than claimed: 592 poses arrived in
4.981 seconds of the bridge's own diagnostic counter, which is 118.9 Hz.
That is the rate the prediction and the render loop have to live with,
and it is close enough to 120 that assuming 120 would have hidden it.
What Android sees when the panel is in its 2D mode, 0x31.
The modes are the important part and the surprising part. There is no
3840-wide mode on this list: the side-by-side modes exist only after the
panel has been switched to 0x32 and has re-advertised itself, which is
why anything choosing a mode has to look again afterwards rather than
once at startup.
And there is no mode above 60 Hz. The refresh rates on offer are 60, 30
and 20 — so a faster panel is not something this one is hiding, at least
not in this mode.
In an extended desktop the display gets a display group and a power group
of its own, which is what lets the phone's screen sleep without taking
the glasses with it.
The refresh rate is the open question, and the measurement says it is not
a bandwidth problem. The panel is rated for 1920x1080 at up to 120 Hz in
2D and 3840x1080 at up to 60 Hz side-by-side; DisplayPort is negotiated on
all four lanes with link training successful. So the bandwidth is there and
the panel can do it, and it is still offering 60 Hz and below.
Which leaves the panel advertising less than it has. That is a thing it is
already known to do: the 3840-wide modes are absent until it is switched
into 0x32 and re-advertises. The mode byte has unexplored neighbours —
0x41 to 0x45 — and the obvious hypothesis is that one of them is the
high-refresh mode. Untested: it needs the glasses attached.

comment: Reading a media library, measured in both power states so the difference
between them is a fact rather than a suspicion.
The suspicion was reasonable: this phone has four slow cores and three
middling ones, the battery saver exists, and a measurement taken at 8%
battery is a measurement of a phone trying to survive. So it was taken
again on the charger with the saver off — and the answer barely moved.
Per entry: 56 ns on battery, 59 ns on mains. Starting eight threads: 3.7 ms
on battery, 4.2 ms on mains. The threaded path loses at every size in both.
So the cost of a thread here is the platform's, not the power mode's, and
the little cores are how the chip is built rather than something being
switched off to save power. Worth knowing, because it means the answer is
stable — and worth having measured, because it was not obvious.
The calibration still re-runs when the power state changes. Not because
this reading demanded it, but because the reading is of one phone and the
code will meet others.
